## Why this matters

PR #490 fixed the immediate red spec by bumping `KNOWN_BELOW_FLOOR_COUNT` from
146 to 149 (R76 §6 grandfathered hygiene path). Both audit lenses (Opus 4.8
and GPT-5.5) independently surfaced a P3 maintainability recommendation:
the pinned literal counter forces a manual bump every time R76 §6 fires
(legitimately back-dated companion or hygiene migration). A content-derived
invariant — e.g. a checked-in manifest of below-floor directory names with
a SHA-pinned content hash — could detect unauthorized back-dated insertions
without recurring manual counter bumps.

The current pinned-literal pattern is also defensible: it deliberately
introduces friction so a human reviews every legitimate back-dated insertion.
This issue is the place to evaluate the tradeoff and either ratify the
current pattern (with rationale documented in the spec) or replace it with
a manifest/hash-based check.

## What's required (by surface)

- **test/roman-coach-reviewed-migration.spec.ts** — either: (a) replace the
  `KNOWN_BELOW_FLOOR_COUNT` literal with a hash check against a checked-in
  below-floor manifest, OR (b) add a comment explicitly ratifying the
  pinned-literal pattern as a deliberate tripwire (with citation to this
  issue and to R76 §6).
- **test/fixtures/below-floor-migrations.json** (option a only) — new
  manifest file; one entry per below-floor migration directory at the
  baseline; pinned with a content hash.
- Decision recorded in the next OPERATOR_DECISIONS_LOG entry.

## Already resolved

- The 146→149 bump itself, in PR #490 (commit 59315faf).
- The PR body's stale line-number references for the FLOOR_TS pin, in the
  PR #490 fixer commit (this issue's sibling change).
